misconceptions.description: Believing data is anonymous as soon as the name column is deleted, ignoring that combined quasi-identifiers can re-identify a person
misconceptions.trigger: learner calls a small dataset anonymous after removing only the name
misconceptions.feedback: Removing the name is not enough. A combination of major, dorm, role, or other details can re-identify one person in a small group.

misconceptions.description: Presenting averages or percentages from a tiny sample as if they were stable group patterns, hiding how few responses there were
misconceptions.trigger: learner reports a percentage over a handful of rows without showing the count
misconceptions.feedback: With a tiny sample, show raw counts like '4 of 7' and suppress or combine groups of one. A small n is not a reliable pattern.

misconceptions.description: Pasting other people's names, emails, or direct identifiers into an external tool without consent or masking
misconceptions.trigger: learner shares a dataset of classmates' personal data with a third-party tool
misconceptions.feedback: Remove or mask direct identifiers before using any external tool. You should not expose others' personal data without consent.
